_comment: What 'illegal_actions = 0' can and cannot mean on the V2 stack, measured across every
metrics file on disk. Three separate channels exist and only the first is the policy's:
illegal_actions      -- the policy chose an action outside the advertised mask
rejection_events     -- the native layer refused an action the mask had advertised
dead_end_reason      -- how an episode ended (empty_action_mask / step_cap / ...)
The env runs in rejection_mode='filter' by default (training/v2_flat_env.py:164,276-290):
a rejected action is removed from that state's mask and the decision is handed back to the
policy, so the step is taken by the policy's NEXT-BEST legal action instead. In this mode
illegal_actions cannot be non-zero for a mask-legal chooser -- the disagreements are real,
but they show up in the second channel.
This is not a contradiction between files: the 861 native_rejection dead ends live in 12
legacy-schema files that have no rejection_events field at all (all from
runs/curriculum_v2/aborted-pre-filter-floor6-095635Z), i.e. an older stack where a
rejection ended the episode. Every current-schema file that counts rejections ends zero

channels._legacy_dirs_note: paths relative to the repository root

by_stage_split._comment: [rejections, episodes, per-episode rate]; stage/split pairs with zero rejections are omitted

established: on the act1 stage the mask and the native layer disagree about 0.53 times per episode (13,245 rejections over 25,000 promotion episodes), and the deepest per-file rate seen is 385 rejections in one 500-episode evaluation

the campaign's reported 'illegal_actions = 0' is therefore partly structural in filter mode: the wrapper prevents the execution rather than observing it, and the underlying disagreements are counted in a different field
the two field populations are explained without hand-waving: legacy files (no rejection_events, 861 native_rejection endings) versus current files (counter present, zero endings)
every figure in this file is emitted by scripts/census_contract_channels.py over the same population, not transcribed by hand
not_established: which phase the rejections land in, and therefore what to fix first -- attributing them needs a per-step recording pass, which has not been run
how much the win-rate and mean-floor numbers would move if the policy had been allowed to execute its first choice: filter mode re-decides, so the counterfactual is not observable from these files
whether the disagreement rate is stable across checkpoints or specific to particular ones
scope: every metrics file on disk, all stages and splits; simulator_act1 label
